transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (HelixPay Platform), Tom Reynolds (HelixPay ML), Elena Gomez (HelixPay PM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): we narrowed model candidates and wrote down a fallback playbook; need access and bench runs.

[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everybody thanks for jumping on, quick agenda — catalog comparison, pinning, rollback playbook, and then bench next steps. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya: doing good, yeah thanks. we had some prod noise last week so i'm keen to make sure the switch plan is tight.
[00:18] Maya: quick note, i'll try to keep the deep infra stuff to the end — we have some KV cache questions.
[00:25] Elena: high level, leadership wants confidence we can swap back within 5 minutes if the model regresses.
[00:32] Jordan: totally, that's the ask. ok model candidates: we ran the initial perf sweep — rdx-7B-q4, rdx-13B-int8, and rdx-6B-fp16 (legacy). the 7B q4 is looking promising on cost but shows a 6-8% drop on our prompt set for completion fidelity vs 13B.
[01:05] Tom: mhm, those fidelity numbers are rough, can you show the per-prompt breakdown? i want to see which intents are hitting lower.
[01:12] Jordan: yeah i'll share the CSV after. quick callout — some of the degradation is on long-form confirmations, not the short auth flows.
[01:20] Priya: for checkout we care a lot about exactness on payment instructions and not hallucinations, so that's a big deal.
[01:27] Maya: technical note — when we pin versions we recommend two things: a canary route at 5% with latency SLO gating, and a soft fallback route that reroutes to a heavier model if safety or hallucination checks fail. the soft fallback is basically a policy-based router in front of the inference pool.
[01:45] Elena: when you say "pin", do you mean pin the exact model artifact (hash) or pin a named slot like rdx-13B-latest?
[01:52] Maya: good question — for this POC we recommend pinning to an artifact hash for the rollout window (say 48–72 hours) and then promote to a named alias after manual QA. hashes give deterministic rollback.
[02:05] Tom: how big are the artifacts differences when you use quantized variants? like rdx-13B-int8 vs rdx-13B-int4? will we need compatibility tests?
[02:13] Jordan: yes typically output drift jumps with different quant schemes; compatibility matrix is needed. we'll provide a short set of automated evals to run.
[02:20] Priya: our compliance team also wants to know about KV cache persistence — are any tokens or PII stored in cache?
[02:27] Maya: no PII should be cached by default. Redwood runtime does prefix/KV cache but we can configure TTLs and scrubbing. side note: sometimes the transcript here says K-V cash which is hilarious — human transcriber thing.
[02:39] Jordan: ha.
[02:41] Maya: back to rollback playbook — primary idea: (1) canary at 5% for 2 hours, monitor quality regressions and latency percentiles, (2) if quality fails, flip 95% traffic to fallback model variant (heavier model) using routing policy, (3) if latency is the issue, move traffic to dedicated pool or increase batch size and re-evaluate. also include an emergency circuit-breaker to revert to last-known-good artifact.
[03:15] Tom: what are the signals for "quality fails"? AUC? BLEU? or custom prompts?
[03:22] Jordan: we use a small prompt-sentinel set (your 500 prompts) and run automatic checks: string matches, safety triggers, and a token-level surprise metric. we'll share the eval harness.
[03:40] Elena: does Redwood provide the rollback API or do we need to implement in our router?
[03:46] Maya: the Redwood control plane supports version pinning and rollbacks via the API — you can call a rollout job, and it supports canary percentages and immediate rollback. for Private customers the control plane can be on your VPC but the api is the same surface.
[03:58] Priya: good. access question — will need test credentials and a temporary service account in our dev VPC.
[04:04] Jordan: noted — action on Priya for VPC access.
[04:08] Tom: bench plan — i'd like to run a 48-hour steady-state A/B with our peak-ish traffic replay. can Redwood simulate traffic shaping?
[04:16] Maya: we can spin up a worker harness to replay your trace or we can instrument the test env and run a real replay. for latency we recommend a 48-hour run to catch tail spikes and GC-like events.
[04:28] Jordan: also we need to test the fallback path under load — route 100% to fallback and run failure injection, see how long the cutover takes.
[04:36] Priya: that's the tabletop drill idea — simulate a model regression and measure our ops time to detect and rollback.
[04:44] Elena: timeline — leadership wants a demo of rollback within two weeks. is that feasible?
[04:49] Maya: yes, assuming we have VPC access and the prompt set by Friday next week.
[04:55] Jordan: ok real quick on cost: rough estimate shows rdx-7B-q4 is ~40% cheaper per token vs 13B-int8, but when you factor in error rates and mitigations the net could be closer. we'll include a cost delta table.
[05:08] Tom: can we get the per-route billing breakdown? we want token-level, per-route for internal chargeback.
[05:14] Jordan: yes that's part of Redwood Console — we'll export token-level breakdown and share.
[05:20] Priya: security checklist — SOC2, KMS, SSO. who owns the KMS integration?
[05:25] Jordan: Redwood supports KMS and HSM integrations; we'll send the SOC2 summary and our KMS integration guide.
[05:32] Elena: any vendor lock concerns if we use Redwood Dedicated vs Private?
[05:36] Maya: Dedicated is managed by us in Redwood infra; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control but requires more ops. for POC we generally start on a hosted/dedicated blend and then revisit Private if needed.
[05:50] Jordan: wrap up — we've got action items: Jordan to send catalog and cost matrix, Maya to run KV-cache microbench, Priya to grant VPC test access, Tom to supply prompts, and we'll schedule the tabletop for 2026-09-30.
[06:05] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.

End of recording
